Project Title:
Cross-Platform E-commerce Revenue Attribution Modeling using Pandas, XGBoost, and Attribution Modeling Algorithms
Reference ID: ai-ml-ds-SrmZNuoOhMk
File Name: cross_platform_ecommerce_revenue_attribution_modeling.py

Short Description:

This project aims to develop an advanced, cross-platform e-commerce revenue attribution model. By leveraging Pandas for data manipulation, XGBoost for predictive modeling, and sophisticated attribution modeling algorithms (including Shapley values and Markov chains), the model seeks to accurately assign revenue credit across multiple marketing channels. This approach facilitates a deeper understanding of customer journeys and enhances marketing ROI by identifying the most effective channels and touchpoints.(arXiv, Erasmus University Thesis Repository, Data Science Blog)

Problem Domain:

  • Domain: E-commerce Marketing Analytics
  • Problem: Attributing revenue accurately across various marketing channels and touchpoints to optimize marketing strategies and budgets.(Plausible Analytics)

Use Cases:

  1. Marketing Channel Optimization: Identify which channels contribute most to conversions and allocate budgets accordingly.
  2. Customer Journey Analysis: Understand the sequence of customer interactions leading to a purchase.
  3. Campaign Performance Evaluation: Assess the effectiveness of marketing campaigns across different platforms.
  4. Predictive Modeling: Forecast future revenue contributions from various channels.(Data Science Blog)

Frameworks and Libraries:

  • Pandas: Data manipulation and analysis.
  • XGBoost: Gradient boosting framework for predictive modeling.
  • scikit-learn: Machine learning utilities.
  • SHAP: Interpretation of machine learning models using Shapley values.
  • NetworkX: Graph-based analysis for Markov models.
  • Matplotlib/Seaborn: Data visualization.(MDPI, Erasmus University Thesis Repository)

Development Lifecycle:

  1. Requirement Analysis: Define objectives and success metrics.
  2. Data Collection: Gather data from various e-commerce platforms and marketing channels.
  3. Data Preprocessing: Clean and prepare data for analysis.
  4. Feature Engineering: Create features representing customer interactions and behaviors.
  5. Model Development: Build predictive models using XGBoost and attribution algorithms.
  6. Model Evaluation: Assess model performance using appropriate metrics.
  7. Deployment: Integrate the model into the business workflow.
  8. Monitoring and Maintenance: Continuously monitor model performance and update as needed.(Erasmus University Thesis Repository, Hrčak)

Python Code:

# cross_platform_ecommerce_revenue_attribution_modeling.py

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import xgboost as xgb
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
import shap
import networkx as nx
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load dataset
data = pd.read_csv('ecommerce_data.csv')

# Preprocessing
data['interaction_time'] = pd.to_datetime(data['interaction_time'])
data.sort_values(by=['user_id', 'interaction_time'], inplace=True)
data['time_diff'] = data.groupby('user_id')['interaction_time'].diff().dt.total_seconds().fillna(0)

# Feature engineering
data['channel_encoded'] = data['channel'].astype('category').cat.codes
features = ['channel_encoded', 'time_diff']
X = data[features]
y = data['conversion']

# Train-test split
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y)

# XGBoost model
model = xgb.XGBClassifier(use_label_encoder=False, eval_metric='logloss')
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Predictions and evaluation
y_pred = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]
auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_pred)
print(f'ROC AUC Score: {auc}')

# SHAP values for interpretability
explainer = shap.Explainer(model)
shap_values = explainer(X_test)
shap.summary_plot(shap_values, X_test)

# Markov chain for attribution
transition_matrix = pd.crosstab(data['channel'], data['next_channel'], normalize='index')
G = nx.from_pandas_adjacency(transition_matrix, create_using=nx.DiGraph())
pos = nx.spring_layout(G)
nx.draw(G, pos, with_labels=True, node_size=2000, node_color='lightblue', arrowsize=20)
plt.title('Markov Chain of Customer Journey')
plt.show()

This code provides a foundational framework for cross-platform e-commerce revenue attribution modeling. It includes data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training with XGBoost, interpretability with SHAP values, and visualization of customer journeys using Markov chains. Further enhancements can be made by integrating real-time data processing, expanding feature sets, and deploying the model within a production environment.
